A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LoRA-One research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic experiments, T5 evaluations on GLUE, LLaMA 2-7B fine-tuning results, and initialization/preconditioning ablations in Section 5 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark results, alignment and transfer experiments, and learning-rate robustness analyses in Section 6 and Appendices B and G. Some comparator results are explicitly attributed to prior work.

M1.justification: v1's primary algorithm uses unweighted singular vectors, offsets the pretrained weights, and applies preconditioned AdamW. v2 replaces it with singular-value-weighted initialization without that offset and ordinary AdamW; this procedure already appeared as Spectral (-) in v1 Algorithm 2. Spectral preconditioning is separately implemented as LoRA-One-P. The former primary implementation and mask-free nonlinear update are removed, so this exceeds renaming.

E1.justification: v2 adds MNIST transfer from odd to even digits and Alpaca instruction fine-tuning evaluated on MMLU general knowledge. GLUE, MetaMathQA/GSM8K, and Code-Feedback/HumanEval remain. These additions extend the represented domains and tasks.

E2.justification: v2 adds PiSSA and LoRA-Pro to the GLUE comparison and LoRA-SB to synthetic comparisons. Multi-step full fine-tuning disappears from the corresponding GLUE and LLM benchmark tables, although it appears in the new MNIST experiment. Table 2's v2 'Full' row represents a single gradient update, not the removed full-fine-tuning baseline.

E3.justification: v2 narrows the main benchmark comparisons to rank 8, revises learning-rate searches and method-specific settings, and adds 8-shot chain-of-thought evaluation and a separate 395K-sample, four-epoch MetaMathQA experiment. The synthetic comparator experiment changes sample size, rank configurations, and target spectrum. QNLI's one-step full-update learning rate changes from 0.02 to 0.05.

E4.justification: v2 adds T5/MRPC alignment measurements, MNIST optimization trajectories, rank-8 approximations of one-step updates, SST-2 learning-rate robustness tests, and a neuron-norm ratio histogram. The earlier CoLA/MRPC rank-by-initialization/preconditioning ablations are removed. The initialization-variance analysis and pretrained-versus-adapted singular-value plots are retained.

E5.justification: Mean/standard-deviation reporting remains, including three-run GLUE results. v2 adds five-seed, 95% confidence intervals for learning-rate robustness and two-run means for the full-data math experiment. Its NLG Table 3 changes the stated run count from three to five, but Appendix Table 6 still lists three, leaving the actual count unresolved.

E6.justification: Numerous results are replaced, added, or removed. One-step QNLI accuracy changes from 69.13 to 76.64 alongside the changed learning rate. New results include LoRA-One's 47.24 on MMLU and 63.80 after four epochs on full-data GSM8K, plus resource measurements. Higher-rank benchmark and ablation entries disappear. Revised LoRA-One scores are not same-setting gains because the procedure and tuning change.

T1.justification: v2 replaces the nonlinear orthonormality/orthogonality and absolute-shift assumptions with neuron-balance and relative-shift conditions. Appendix D replaces Hermite-based population-gradient arguments with angular ReLU-gradient analysis, changing initialization scaling and convergence bounds. The smoothed-gradient theorem and proof are removed, and linear alignment analysis is specialized to equal step sizes. The linear convergence results are retained in Appendix C.

C1.justification: The central claims about subspace alignment, spectral initialization, and convergence remain. v2 adds an explicit introductory claim of competitive performance at nearly LoRA's time and memory cost, centers the contribution on spectral initialization, and drops the introductory claim of stronger guarantees through a modified gradient update.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands the explanation of competing methods' limitations: LoRA-GA's weight offset introduces a biased target, its approximation neglects a quadratic step-size term, and LoRA-SB restricts subspace adaptation. Practical preconditioning guidance shifts from the earlier emphasis on high ranks toward robustness to poorly chosen learning rates. New results also receive interpretations concerning reasoning, knowledge retention, and stability.

D1.justification: Appendix G adds method- and dataset-specific optimized learning rates, batch sizes, scaling parameters, prompting information, and settings for the added experiments. v2 also reports training time and memory. Conversely, the earlier spectral-initializer tuning tables and explicit gradient-averaging implementation description are removed. These materially change the available reproduction information.

R1.justification: v2 expands positioning against recent LoRA theory, including Liu, Kim, and Xu et al., and connects the work to one-gradient-step feature-learning research. The previously acknowledged concurrent LoRA-SB work receives a substantive methodological critique and comparison. New analytical discussion also sharpens the distinction from LoRA-GA; these changes exceed bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, contributions, related work, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. Algorithms/discussion and experiments become separate sections, linear convergence exposition moves into the appendix, and a new preconditioning appendix reorganizes the presentation. Proof sketches and the nonlinear exposition are substantially revised.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column main text and substantially redesigns its displays: a new three-panel overview, restructured benchmark tables, resource-cost reporting, epoch comparisons, confidence-band plots, and a histogram. Earlier rank-ablation displays disappear; the toy trajectories are reduced and relocated, while the singular-value plots move to Appendix G.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the connection between theory and practice: the primary implementation follows the spectral construction, alignment is tested on T5, and stronger comparator coverage, learning-rate robustness tests, and measured resource costs directly examine central claims. These gains outweigh the loss of rank ablations and full-fine-tuning benchmark controls. The conflicting NLG run counts remain a material reporting weakness, and revised scores should not be interpreted as controlled improvements over v1.
